svg.text: MPx Screen: Turbidity Pre-screen + Fine Filter + Optical Confirmation
Every batch is tested first. Clear water goes straight to the tank in seconds; cloudy water is routed through coarse and fine filters, the membrane is checked by camera, then stored.
Inlet and outlet are both on top, as asked; the device never needs to be lifted onto a tap.
C · How each batch is routed
~50 mL batch, settles for a few seconds
Repeats until the funnel is empty.
sloped; sheds into a trap pocket
e.g. 5–10 µm; plastics stay on top
tip the unit to pour, like a teapot
Schematic, not to scale. Gravity moves the water; only the valve, sensor and
Filtered-out plastics stay inside the module: on the membrane and in the trap pocket.
1 · Pull the module out; the lid shutter closes.
2 · Optional: send the membrane to MPx Detect
3 · Seal membrane + pocket contents in the
disposal pouch. Never rinse them down a drain.
4 · Wash the steel mesh; fit a new membrane.
A clear reading is not proof.
A few microplastics barely change turbidity, so a
clear batch can still carry some [2]. Keep the
threshold low, and send every Nth clear batch
through the filters as a spot check.
Turbidity can't tell plastic from silt.
The camera check helps (size and shape); a Nile Red
mode would make it plastic-specific, as in FLOro [1].
Settling speed can also separate plastic from
A fine membrane under gravity may take minutes
per litre. That is exactly the time the pre-screen
Sensor, valve and camera run on a battery (USB-C).
Add a UV-C stage in the tank if that matters.
Turbidity method: nephelometric, 860 nm light, 90° detection [4].
[1] Rermborirak et al. (2025). Low-cost portable microplastic detection system integrating Nile Red staining with YOLOv8 (FLOro). J. Hazard. Mater. Adv. 19, 100787.

[2] Govindarajan et al. (2025). Tracking microplastic pathways: real-time IoT monitoring for water quality and public health. MethodsX 15, 103674. [5] Abimbola et al. (2024). In-situ detection of microplastics in the aquatic environment: a systematic review. Sci. Total Environ. 934, 173111.

[3] Kulkarni, A. (2025). Economical and novel microplastic detection using an Arduino-based turbidity sensor. Preprint, doi:10.22541/au.176252971.19402178/v1. [4] ISO 7027-1:2016. Water quality: determination of turbidity.
